Stability is dominated by the ability to form an intramolecular O–H···N hydrogen bond and by the avoidance of close non-bonded contacts / eclipsed torsions. For every conformer the hydroxyl oxygen atom is atom 15 and the hydroxyl hydrogen is atom 16, the amine nitrogen is atom 7. O···N distances were estimated from the coordinates and H···N distances for the O–H donor were estimated. Short O···N ~2.7–2.9 Å with H···N ~2.2–2.5 Å indicates a viable 5- to 6-membered H-bonded ring, the hallmark of the most stable geometries. Conformer 28 has the shortest O···N ≈2.72 Å and the shortest H···N ≈2.17 Å, followed by 25 at O···N ≈2.74 Å H···N ≈2.22 Å. Conformers 6, 11 and 26 also show O···N ≈2.75 Å with H···N ≈2.21–2.23 Å and very compact H-bonded rings, placing them next. Conformers 19, 3, 20, 17, 21, 24, 14, 2, 27, 8, 5, 9, 7, 30, 10, 1 and 16 all keep O···N <3.0 Å with H···N in the 2.27–2.65 Å range, i.e. an intramolecular H-bond is present but the ring is progressively looser and the overall torsion pattern shows more gauche interactions. The eight conformers 18, 13, 23, 29, 15, 4, 22 and 12 have O···N ≈3.67–3.68 Å, far beyond H-bond range, so no O–H···N stabilization is possible; they also display extended backbones with the donor and acceptor on opposite faces of the chain and are expected to suffer more steric crowding between the alkyl arms. Within each group differences are sub-kcal and depend on fine rotamer details that cannot be resolved reliably from coordinates alone, so the ordering inside the H-bonded set and inside the non H-bonded set is uncertain. The permutation below follows decreasing H-bond quality, i.e. increasing O···N / H···N distance, with the eight non-H-bonded structures placed at the bottom.

The only large-amplitude degrees of freedom are rotations about C5–C6, C6–C7, C7–N and C5–C18, which move the alcohol –CH2OH group relative to the amide. The most stabilizing intramolecular interaction is the alcohol O19 acting as H-bond acceptor from the amide N8–H12 and the alcohol H20 donating to the amide C=O10, i.e. a compact HO···N/C=O close contact that closes a 7- to 9-membered pseudoring. Because the amide geometry is conserved, the N8···O19 separation is an excellent proxy for that close contact: short N···O means the –CH2OH can be folded back onto the amide and an N–H···O or O–H···O=C H-bond can form, long N···O means the alcohol is extended away from the polar amide and no H-bond is possible. Steric clash checks show no obviously eclipsed heavy-atom contacts in the set; the ranking is therefore dominated by the N8···O19 distance with the additional preference for a short H20···O10 contact when it occurs. Computed N8···O19 distances are ~2.81–5.26 Å. The smallest values are 6 and 24 at ~2.81 Å, followed by 10 ~2.82 Å, 18 ~2.90 Å, 25 ~2.91 Å, 12 ~2.92 Å, 15 ~2.92 Å and 19 ~2.93 Å, all indicating a well formed alcohol···amide H-bond. The longest N···O distances are 17 and 11 >5.2 Å where the alcohol is fully extended away from the amide. The ordering is robust for the extremes; conformers with N···O within ~0.1 Å of each other, e.g. 6/24 and 14/1/7, are essentially degenerate on the level of a distance-only estimate and the final order among those neighbours is uncertain without a proper energy evaluation. Steric/eclipsing contributions are secondary and do not overturn the H-bond trend.

reason: The 22-atom set is C6H13NO2, i.e. a flexible hydroxy-amino motif with two hydroxyl oxygens that can H-bond to each other and to the amine. Across the 30 geometries the atom ordering is conserved: O7 is the first hydroxyl O with its H8, O20 is the second hydroxyl O with its H21 and N15 is the amine nitrogen with its H16. The most important stability discriminator for a flexible chain of this size is the ability to form an intramolecular O–H···O hydrogen bond. That is essentially captured by the O7···O20 separation; an O···O of ~2.75–2.85 Å allows an O–H···O with H···O ~1.8–2.1 Å, whereas O···O > ~3.5 Å precludes a productive H-bond and forces the chain into extended, higher-energy conformations. The same O···O metric correlates with the N···O contacts that give a secondary NH···O stabilisation. Computations of O7···O20 from the XYZ coordinates give a clear bimodal distribution: ~19 conformers sit in the 2.76–2.82 Å ideal H-bond window, ~5 conformers are in a moderate 3.0–3.8 Å window where the O–H···O is weak or absent, and six conformers are >4.2 Å with no intramolecular O···O contact at all – i.e. extended, strained geometries. Within the good window the shortest O···O distances are the most stabilising, with Conformer 12 at ~2.76 Å and a very short N···O20 ~2.7 Å giving a clear O–H···O plus NH···O motif, followed by 24, 21, 1, 20, 10, 6, 13, 27, etc. Conformer 29, 16, 22, 30, 11, 14 are also in the ideal window but with slightly longer O···O. Conformer 7, 9, 2, 4 sit at the upper edge of the ideal window. The moderate group 15 ~3.02 Å, 5 ~3.40 Å, 23 ~3.65 Å, 8 ~3.80 Å, 18 ~3.85 Å retain some contacts but the H-bond is weak and the chains are more exposed. The six bad geometries 25 ~4.23 Å, 3 ~4.24 Å, 26 ~4.34 Å, 28 ~4.42 Å, 17 ~4.49 Å, 19 ~4.89 Å have O7···O20 far apart, no intramolecular H-bond, larger non-bonded exposure and, in several cases, eclipsed backbone torsions. The differences among the ~19 good conformers are subtle – O···O varies by only ~0.06 Å – and the exact order inside that band is uncertain without a full energy evaluation, but the separation between the good, moderate and bad O···O groups is robust.
